bytes necessary to hold the string data coming in.

div.span: Interface that classes must implement if they want to serialize OTLP objects such as LogRecords and Spans. Used to ensure that classes don't forget to implement a serialization method for a specific type. The class should keep track of the serialized value internally and provide it as an output rather than making the methods "pure" where they return a value.

text.tspan: Interface that classes must implement if they want to serialize OTLP objects
such as LogRecords and Spans. Used to ensure that classes don't forget to
implement a serialization method for a specific type. The class should keep
track of the serialized value internally and provide it as an output rather than
making the methods "pure" where they return a value.

div.span: Used to export data using ProtoJSON to an endpoint. Because an exporter can serialize both logs and traces, it is responsible for managing an internal "busy" bit so that it doesn't have two requests to the same otlp collector going simultainously, thus internally syncronizing log and trace exports.

text.tspan: Used to export data using ProtoJSON to an endpoint. Because an exporter
can serialize both logs and traces, it is responsible for managing an internal
"busy" bit so that it doesn't have two requests to the same otlp collector
going simultainously, thus internally syncronizing log and trace exports.

div.span: The FB_Logger instances should be built using the FB_LoggerProvider, which implements the factory pattern via the GetLogger API. The getLogger method MUST take the parameters necessary to instantiate an FB_InstrumentationScope instance. The FB_InstrumentationScope defines the "module" or "vertical slice" of for which the logger is responsible, for example if a system is instrumented and it contains pumps and valves, perhaps each device would have a scope, and then the service (in a domain modeling sense) could have it's own logger that emits process specific logs.

text.tspan: The FB_Logger instances should be built using the
FB_LoggerProvider, which implements the factory pattern via the
GetLogger API. The getLogger method MUST take the parameters
necessary to instantiate an FB_InstrumentationScope instance. The
FB_InstrumentationScope defines the "module" or "vertical slice" of
for which the logger is responsible, for example if a system is
instrumented and it contains pumps and valves, perhaps each device
would have a scope, and then the service (in a domain modeling
sense) could have it's own logger that emits process specific logs.

div.span: An FB_LoggerProvider MUST implement the Get Logger API. Additionally the FB_LoggerProvider must be intialized with a instance of an FB_Resource. The resource describes the highest level "host" or "bubble" that is emitting the logs. In the case of PLC logging the resource would contain information regarding the device sending data to the server.

text.tspan: An FB_LoggerProvider MUST implement the Get Logger API.
Additionally the FB_LoggerProvider must be intialized with a
instance of an FB_Resource. The resource describes the
highest level "host" or "bubble" that is emitting the logs. In the
case of PLC logging the resource would contain information
regarding the device sending data to the server.

the documentation with no corresponding
class diagram, such as
FB_InstrumentationScope, FB_Resource.

specified are PODO classes that simply
manage the life cycle of the data with
convenience methods like free() and
delete() to help manage deallocating
memory.
